The concrete first target is the worst-case number G_3(n) of distinct monomial initial ideals of a length-n polynomial quotient in three variables, over all fields. First audit the strongest relevant primary literature and the repository's unfinished lattice-shadow work; distinguish a genuinely new theorem from a classical geometric corollary before using it. A draft, a bounded priority review, isolated examples, a minor refinement, or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete this goal. Along s_j(tau)=s_j(0)+tau*q_j, group costs are discretely convex. uniform_proofs: Let a rank-r matroid have the entire ground {a in N_0^d:m.a<L} and allow replacing any selected element by any unselected element of no larger additive valuation. At a tied feasible exchange e to f at positive cost t, every unselected element with valuation at most max(v(e),v(f)) is also a feasible replacement for e. Optimality puts all points strictly cheaper than t in that valuation prefix into the basis. There are at most r-1 of them.

The closed cheap prefix is an intersection of two positive halfspaces in the orthant. Floor-halving maps it to the strict prefix with fibers at most 2^d; an explicit 1/d inner grid bounds its box by d^d times its size. Thus every raw tied feasible exchange satisfies product_i(|f_i-e_i|+1)<=(2*d)^d*(r-1), uniformly in the ground size, truncation and valuation vector. The primitive direction satisfies the same bound.

Classical matroid exchange geometry makes every positive cone facet one of those directions. A single hyperbolic cross has O_d(r*log(r+1)^(d-1)) possible normals; the classical central arrangement gives O_d(r^(d-1)*log(r+1)^((d-1)^2)) positive bases. A shared list of positive integer weights of that size samples all such rank-r matroids, with coordinate heights O_d(r^(d-1)) by cofactors. Shared-list sampling and the Hilbert-zonotope method are prior art; the extra content is the rank-sized direction estimate under the lowering hypothesis.

Every explicit quotient I_(L,m) from the ordered exponential construction satisfies the lowering property, in every fixed dimension. Its actual length is n=L-max_k(k-nu_m(k)). The entire characteristic-zero family, including unequal valuations and embedding dimension three, therefore has the generic polynomial exponent d-1 up to logarithmic factors. In three variables its count is O(n^2*log(n+1)^4). This closes the whole construction as a power-separation route.

Each subset meeting the rank inequalities has a minor nonzero at the explicit exponential point. Its primitive wall normal (p,-q,0) has product (p+1)*(q+1), quadratic in length for consecutive p,q.
